text:
Utah has one of the better five-on-five games in the league and a record that doesn't show it. The Mammoth take 57% of the expected goals at five-on-five (the quality of chances for and against) and 54% overall, yet they are 10-8-2 with 22 points. The gap is in goal: Utah has allowed about nine more goals than its chances predicted, and our numbers have them two and a half points short of what they've earned.

The last week is a different story, and the chances back it. The Mammoth are winless in four (0-2-2), outscored 15-9, with only 42% of the expected goals in those games. Sebastian Cossa has an .869 save percentage and is 4.3 goals worse than expected over his last five starts. Injuries explain part of it: Dylan Guenther is out two to four weeks, Nate Schmidt is on injured reserve, and Logan Cooley (13 points in his last ten) is day to day with an upper-body injury.

André Tourigny still has pieces that work. Anders Lee, Barrett Hayton and Kailer Yamamoto have taken 74% of the expected goals together, and rookie defenseman Dmitri Simashev is producing above his chances. The top pair of Mikhail Sergachev and MacKenzie Weegar is the puzzle: a 57% expected goals share, but outscored 13-6.

Sergachev's name has also surfaced in reports linking Utah to Nikita Kucherov. Our numbers still give the Mammoth a 69% chance at the playoffs.
headline: Mammoth outplay teams, then lose them in net
